component: Visible threaded DB view row deletion

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: Deleting an expanded root collapses the old visible children, removes the stale row, adds the promoted root and expands it when more than one child remains. A non-root deletion instead saves its old level, removes that row and shifts only the following run of deeper descendants left by one level. A single change notification covers that run. The two added local-folder tests assert root promotion and one descendant-level shift; they do not directly establish every selection, notification or failure-path outcome.
title: Threaded deletion handles root promotion and descendant levels in separate paths
